answer: Under EigenTrust-style scoring, reputation decays exponentially with a fixed half-life, so an identity must provide sustained, reciprocated honest service to retain influence. A newly spawned sybil has few trusted incoming paths and near-zero eigenvector centrality; splitting activity among aliases does not create credible transitive support, so the identities cannot pass consensus merely by appearing. Like a karst channel, trust follows established paths, not a sudden zenith of claims or a reef of fresh accounts.
